criteria.criterion: Recovery extension per option (b): `binding_walk.py`'s unbound arm detects a marked-but-unstored key (rebar-id label equal to the deterministic inbound local id; no binding-store entry for that id; no local ticket) and replays the adopt through the existing inbound-create leaf, instead of standing down on the L10 guard. `compute_binding_walk_mutations` complexity does not increase (guard swapped one-for-one into a helper).

A RED-first regression test simulating the lost-final-push runner: runner 1 adopts (CREATE event + binding written, label stamped), the final push is rejected and ALL local state is discarded; runner 2 (fresh store, fresh tracker) sees the labeled snapshot — the walk emits the replay adopt and applying it re-materialises the local ticket + binding under the SAME deterministic local id with no duplicate label. Confirmed failing (walk stands down, adopted == []) before the fix.

Existing L10/L11 protections preserved: foreign/ghost markers, multi-marker keys, keys whose marked id still has a store entry, and keys whose marked local ticket still exists all keep standing down; retired keys still skip. Existing tests `test_class_b_labeled_key_not_double_bound` and `test_class_b_empty_rebar_id_marker_is_adopted` unchanged and green.
bridge fsck continues to alert unbound_jira on the class until healed — no suppression added anywhere (fsck code untouched; post-heal the key is bound so the alert clears by becoming true).

Bug 'Reconcile stamps Jira rebar-id label before local adoption is durably published — push-rejected ephemeral runs strand unhealable unbound_jira drift' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces.
